A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2D research, and their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. Extracted text recovers the content obscured by overlapping prose and algorithms on v4 page 5.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original eICU and Lacuna-100 experiments, including classification errors, membership-inference attacks, and computation times.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original classification AUCs, two membership-inference attacks, noise comparisons, and computation times on both datasets.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain gradient-descent training, checkpoint rewinding or proximal checkpoint reconstruction, gradient descent on retained data, and Gaussian output perturbation. The revised experimental configurations do not introduce a new R2D procedure.

E1.justification: The eICU and Lacuna-100 classification tasks, user-level deletion, and OOD populations are retained. V4 adds a limited threat-scenario extension through MIA-U, whose attacker accesses both original and unlearned model outputs; v2 evaluates attacks using only post-unlearning outputs.

E2.justification: V2 evaluates R2D against Hessian-Free Unlearning and Constrained Newton Step. V4 retains these comparators and adds evaluated Finetune, Fisher Forgetting, and SCRUB baselines in Tables 2–3 and Appendix B, substantially expanding comparison beyond certified methods.

E3.justification: Reported R2D settings change to constant 0.01 step sizes, larger batches (512/256 to 2048/512), longer training (52/82 to 78/270 epochs), and a smaller eICU model (Table 4). Model utility changes from error to AUC. Certified-baseline epsilon sweeps shift from 10–40 to 10,000–10,000,000; v4 also adds fixed-noise comparisons and revises MIA inputs, cross-validation, and original-model perturbation controls.

E4.justification: V2's noiseless rewinding study becomes comparisons with and without noise under both classic MIA and MIA-U in v4 Figure 4. V4 adds tests of leakage exposed by pre/post-model comparisons and noise-versus-privacy/rewinding analyses. The Lacuna-100 epsilon-sensitivity panels in v2 Figures 1–2 are no longer reported.

E5.justification: V2 specifies five seeds, except single-seed baseline comparisons, and reports averages. V4 removes those explicit training-run counts but introduces MIA standard deviations across cross-validation trials in Tables 8–11, specifying ten five-fold repetitions and 100 classic-MIA undersampling repetitions. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in independent training runs.

E6.justification: V2's error tables at epsilon 40 and delta 0.1 are replaced by expanded AUC comparisons at fixed noise or without noise. New Lacuna-100 MIA-U results include 0.6779 for R2D at 37% rewinding and 0.8461 for HF (v4 Table 10). Reported R2D Lacuna-100 learning time changes from 1.47 to 4.57 hours alongside changed training budgets, so this is not a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: Equation 6 corrects the PL definition from one-half the squared norm of f(x) to one-half the squared gradient norm. The principal bounds and proofs are otherwise retained: v2's empirical-risk Corollary 3.5 moves to v4 Corollary A.5, and its population-risk Corollary 3.6 becomes Corollary 3.3.

C1.justification: The first-order, black-box, certified nonconvex-unlearning contribution and PL guarantees remain central. V4 broadens the empirical superiority claims to include non-certified methods and defense against MIA-U, particularly in the introduction, contribution list, and conclusion.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's existing caveats about implementation approximations and distribution-sensitive MIAs, v4 explicitly acknowledges that useful utility requires very large epsilon, discusses the convergence costs of constant-step large-batch training, and recognizes non-certified methods' utility advantages (Appendix C). Appendix B.1.1 also expands explanations of attack behavior and the effects of perturbing original models.

D1.justification: V4 adds eICU table joins and feature lists, dataset-access instructions, detailed attack construction, newly disclosed baseline optimizers and CNS parameters, and implementation information for the new baselines. Hardware/software descriptions are revised. Conversely, v4 Table 4 leaves the previously reported Lacuna-100 L and G estimates blank; the common anonymous R2D repository link is retained.

R1.justification: Most related work and certified-method positioning are retained. V4 adds Chen et al.'s 2021 'When Machine Unlearning Jeopardizes Privacy' to motivate MIA-U and broadens empirical positioning against non-certified methods. Qiao et al.'s changed title and publication details correspond to the retained HF work.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially rewritten and reorganized from six subsections into Setup and Results. Proofs are consolidated, the empirical-risk corollary moves into the appendix, and experimental and related-work appendices are reordered. Dedicated limitations, broader impacts, and a conference checklist further change the document structure.

P2.justification: The main text switches from two columns to one, and experimental displays are extensively redesigned: error plots give way to AUC and dual-attack tables, with reorganized sensitivity figures and appendix displays. V4 also introduces a conspicuous layout defect on page 5, where the introductory paragraph overlaps Algorithms 1 and 2.

improvement.justification: The added MIA-U and non-certified comparisons address the stronger evaluation deferred in v2 Appendix D.3; MIA variability estimates and explicit practical limitations make the evidence easier to assess. These benefits provide a limited overall gain, tempered by removed training-run disclosures, accuracy claims broader than Table 2 supports, and the algorithm/prose overlap on v4 page 5.
